title: Make the test suite robust to colorized argparse output

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Python 3.14 colorizes argparse usage and error text when color is enabled (a tty, or `FORCE_COLOR`). Many tests assert plain substrings like `usage: slicer` and `unrecognized arguments`, so in a shell with `FORCE_COLOR` set (as this project's dev environment has), about 35 tests in `test_ai`, `test_cli`, and `test_errors` fail on embedded ANSI escapes even though the code is correct. CI or a developer with color forced on would see a red suite for no real reason.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `tests/support.py` (the in-process `TempRepo.run`) or the affected assertions
- `src/slicer/cli.py` if color is disabled at the parser instead

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. With `FORCE_COLOR=3` in the environment, `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` passes: the usage/error assertions still match.
2. A parser error's captured stderr contains a plain, uncolored `usage:` line and message.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Neutralize color for slicer's own parser output rather than stripping it after the fact. Prefer the source: have the in-process test runner clear `FORCE_COLOR` / set `NO_COLOR` for the call, or build the parser with color disabled when output is captured or not a tty. Keep colored help available for real interactive use if the project wants it. Do not weaken the assertions to accept ANSI.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: The suite passes both with and without `FORCE_COLOR` set, and no test asserts on ANSI escape codes. `slicer check` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit. Do not tag or push.
